name: New Navel
slug: New Navel is a familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
description: New Navel is a place the party has visited before. Carlkin's lighthouse is there, and trade caravans run from New Navel to the party's tavern in Langdale.

log.summary: Ord, Sylan, Gerk, and Dana enter New Navel and go to Carlkin's lighthouse, which they have been inside once or twice. Trade caravans run from New Navel to the party's tavern in Langdale.
notes: Ord, Sylan, Gerk, and Dana enter New Navel and go to Carlkin's lighthouse, a place they have been inside once or twice.
Trade caravans run from New Navel to the party's tavern in Langdale.

log.summary: At midday on the party's sixth day, New Navel is busy with ordinary traffic and with traders coming through for trade tied to the town. The group with Sylan is outside Carlkin's lighthouse, and Ord, Sylan, and Gerk then go to the pub, with a day and a half left on the current clock. The road between the tavern and New Navel runs near the mis-aimed doorway, about a quarter mile southwest of the tavern, where three human traders with a mule cart were traveling.
notes: Midday on the party's sixth day. People are out on ordinary business, and traders are coming through for trade associated with New Navel. The group with Sylan is outside Carlkin's lighthouse, then Ord, Sylan, and Gerk go to the pub. A day and a half remains on the current clock.
The road between the tavern and New Navel passes near the mis-aimed doorway, about a quarter mile southwest of the tavern. Three human traders with a mule cart were traveling that road.

log.summary: Plymouth asks to be dropped at New Navel and walks toward it on his own. As Ledzbika dematerializes, he reaches toward New Navel. Sylan thinks he has to spend a couple of days there as a ghost detective because of restless souls he picked up, and Gerk tells him to do that at Carlkin's house.
notes: Plymouth asks to be dropped here and walks toward it on his own.

Ledzbika reaches toward New Navel as he dematerializes. Sylan thinks he has to spend a couple of days here as a ghost detective because of restless souls he picked up. Gerk tells him to do that at Carlkin's house.

log.summary: Once Neville, New Navel was a prison of sorts that people escaped without realizing. The dead could pass on normally or return as celestial echoes. Sheriff Haldor ties that loosely and uncertainly to a sea-associated elder god and says this is why undead are not rampant. Sylan's six spirits are locals with unfinished business still walking the town; he thinks his last pass toward Carlkin's collected some. He remembers no mayor, only Haldor. Shades and Trades sits mid-town, so he waits outside to avoid collecting more dead. The center market has living vendors, the sheriff's house and a tavern southwest, and stalls selling wicker animals and only geese. Dragons by the lighthouse draw a crowd; Gerk goes in alone while the others fly there. Extradimensional and interdimensional doors, spirit-taking, and summoning undead are forbidden in town; magic and doorway tricks stay outside, and a spirit lantern must be hidden or confiscated. Carlkin reported yesterday's door; his commons is inside the limit. No recent missing persons; a handful to a dozen deaths in six or seven months, travelers included. Mines across the lake are reopening. Sylan suspects a soul trap or a failed search and has no time to pursue it.
notes: The six spirits associated with Sylan are people from New Navel with unfinished business there. Spirits are still walking the town. Sylan thinks his last pass, including the way to Carlkin's, collected some of them.

Sylan remembers a sheriff who watched the town and does not remember a mayor. The sheriff is Haldor. Shades and Trades sits in the middle of town, so Sylan waits outside rather than cross town and collect more dead, then later plans to walk the long way through.

The town center has a small open market of living vendors. The sheriff's house and a tavern are southwest of that market. One stall sells wicker animals. Two doors down, another vendor sells only geese.
Dragons landing near the lighthouse draw a crowd. Gerk goes in alone while the others fly to the lighthouse.

Once known as Neville. Residents and travelers escaped without realizing it was a prison of sorts. People who died could pass on normally or return as celestial echoes. Haldor ties that loosely and uncertainly to a sea-associated elder god, and says this is why undead are not rampant.

Extradimensional and interdimensional doors are prohibited inside the city limits. Magic practice is directed to the forest outside. Spirit-taking and summoning undead are forbidden. A magical lantern that brings spirits must stay hidden or be confiscated. Haldor also wants other doorway tricks and general commotion kept outside town.
Carlkin's commons is inside the limit. He reported yesterday's door to the sheriff.
Trigash Forest is a couple of miles away. Fliers covered that distance much faster than Gerk and Sylan did on foot. The Trigash beacon was obvious from town.

No recent missing persons. Deaths over the last six or seven months are a handful, maybe a dozen including travelers. Haldor calls it a frontier town on a rough road. Mines on the other side of the lake are opening again and drawing competition and traffic.
Sylan suspects either that the town traps souls or that he has failed to find lost souls. He decides he does not have time to pursue that now.
